original_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2 with finite singular set Sing(F). Is it true that every leaf L of F meets Sing(F)?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.1 ("Exceptional minimal set problem"): for every leaf L of a holomorphic foliation \mathcal F on \mathbb{P}^2, does \overline{L}\cap\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)\neq\varnothing? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient surface \mathbb{P}^2, the presence of a finite singular set \operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F), and the universal quantifier over all leaves. It is also clearly aiming at the paper's exceptional minimal set problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper's question is about the topological closure \overline{L} of a leaf, not the leaf L itself. A genuine leaf lies in \mathbb{P}^2\setminus\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F), so asking whether L itself meets \operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F) is not the intended formulation.
The ambient field should be made explicit: \mathbb{P}^2 means the complex projective plane \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}).

It is better to say that \mathcal F is a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on \mathbb{P}^2, and that L ranges over leaves of \mathcal F in \mathbb{P}^2\setminus\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F).
The closure \overline{L} should be specified as the topological closure taken in the ambient projective plane \mathbb{P}^2.
The paper poses this as an open problem with no added degree restriction, hyperbolicity assumption, or invariant-curve hypothesis; those should not be inserted into the refined question.
The finiteness of \operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F) is background notation in the paper's setup for this problem, not a special extra hypothesis narrowing the question.
refined_question: Let \mathcal F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective plane \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}), and let \operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F) denote its finite singular set. For every leaf L of \mathcal F (so L\subset \mathbb{P}^2\setminus\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)), must its topological closure \overline{L}\subset \mathbb{P}^2 satisfy \overline{L}\cap\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)\neq\varnothing?
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper's exceptional minimal set problem. In the introduction, the authors phrase the motivating question informally as whether leaves always cluster at singular points, and in Section 5 they formalize that question as Problem 5.1. The crucial correction is the missing closure bar: the paper's problem concerns \overline{L}, not L. This is also consistent with the paragraph immediately after Problem 5.1, where the authors discuss constructing a directed positive \partial\bar\partial-closed current supported on \overline{L} and explain a partial positive answer when the foliation admits a directed positive closed current, in particular when it has an invariant algebraic curve. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
